cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Pass Me the Authority
cards.instruction: Get someone to transfer authority publicly by naming you as the person who decides what happens next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Hand me the hall key and tell everyone I'm now in charge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't I just give you the key? My retirement taxi's waiting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. The door will understand. The committee needs words.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're outside asking me whether to cancel Saturday's dance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them I decide whether it goes ahead. Then ask me, in front of them. Your taxi can be my first approval.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 commands the handover, A3 rejects a merely physical transfer, and A5 makes B request permission publicly before departure, joining presumed top rank to transfer.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 taxi urgency prompts A3 insistence on words; B4 dance question gives A5 an actual public demonstration. A5 taxi approval compresses granting B leave rather than operating the taxi.

relationship.evidence: B2 retiree wants to leave and B4 committee still treats B as decision maker; both supply real pressure.

heightening.evidence: B4 live dance question causes A5 to demand not just a declaration but a public question to A, then B departure as first approval.

specificity.evidence: A1 hall key and B2 retirement establish succession; B4 committee outside provides the public audience missing from a private handover.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 door understands contrasts key with words, while A5 makes the waiting taxi depend on the ceremony; stock prefix remains cumbersome.
